card: Wallet transaction funding (`fundrawtransaction`) fails to enforce caller-specified `max_tx_weight` when provided preset inputs already cover the target amount. Because coin selection exits early, the wallet's post-selection guard only checked against `MAX_STANDARD_TX_WEIGHT` (400,000 WU), creating transactions that exceed requested constraints. This PR updates the post-selection check to use the caller-configured maximum weight and adds regression tests.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to code or tests; this matches the previous description version with full patch diff confirmed.
evidence: PR description: 'I reproduced this with 10 legacy inputs and max_tx_weight=4000. Funding succeeded even though the transaction was 6,168 WU after signing. Same result with both add_inputs=false and add_inputs=true.'
Regression test added in `test/functional/wallet_fundrawtransaction.py` fails before the change and passes with it.
problem: Callers of `fundrawtransaction` (and underlying wallet funding logic) specifying `max_tx_weight` can receive transactions that exceed their requested weight limit if the provided preset inputs already cover the target value. Coin selection returns early, skipping its weight checks, and the final guard check fell back to the 400,000 WU standard network limit.

risk.why: A flaw in wallet transaction creation weight checks could cause valid transactions to fail creation or allow oversized transactions that fail relay or break caller weight constraints.

summary: Enforce the configured `max_tx_weight` in wallet transaction creation when preset inputs already cover the payment amount. Previously, bypassing coin selection caused the final guard in `CreateTransactionInternal` to evaluate only `MAX_STANDARD_TX_WEIGHT` instead of `coin_selection_params.m_max_tx_weight`.
